name: Ospedale degli Innocenti

dates.note: The Institute's own museum page dates Brunelleschi's site direction: 'Brunelleschi directed the Ospedale's construction site from 1419 to 1427'. The node's exemplar note gives 'begun 1419, completed 1445', which is the whole complex rather than Brunelleschi's own campaign. Both are recorded.

quotes.text: Engaged in that same period in the construction of the dome of Santa Maria del Fiore, Brunelleschi developed a peculiar language for the building, using materials such as pietra serena and plaster to design a space marked by columns, capitals, arches and vaults, which in the recovery of classical elements anticipates a distinctive feature of Florentine Renaissance architecture. Specially conceived for the reception and care of abandoned children, it was defined by architect Giovanni Michelucci as "a palace for children. "
quotes.page: Museo degli Innocenti, 'Architecture' page, opening paragraph. The stray space before the closing quotation mark is as the page prints it.

quotes.text: Brunelleschi directed the Ospedale's construction site from 1419 to 1427, building the External Loggia 1, the Church of Santa Maria degli Innocenti 2 and the children's dormitory (today's Salone Brunelleschi) 3. He designs, finally, the Cortile degli Uomini 6.

THE NODE'S OWN CLAIM ABOUT THIS BUILDING IS NOT CHECKABLE FROM ANY REGISTER TEXT READ HERE: the exemplar note says 'an arcade of nine bays in which the column height, arch span and bay depth are all the same dimension', and the Institute's own architecture page states no bay count and no dimension whatever. The one figure the page gives is the diameter of a della Robbia roundel.
